extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and sports fans (and sports reporters)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and evaluating newspaper game recaps and short-form sports analysis (football/baseball/crew) describing team performance, individual play, strategy, and statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rushing yards and first downs (team statistical superiority)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statistics of play bear out the superiority of the Yale team. Yale gained 298 yards by rushing to Princeton’s 145 and made 15 first downs to the Tigers’ 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rushing yardage and number of first downs as primary measures of ground-game dominance in football recaps; include comparative figures to show superiority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-passing effectiveness (attempts vs. yards gained)
rubrics_metrics.description: Yale essayed seven forward passes to Princeton’s 10, gaining 69 yards to Princeton’s 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report not just pass attempts but yardage gained — a team may throw more but gain nothing; include notable long spirals or passes described as 'reaching the proportions of a kick.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Punting frequency and average return/gain
rubrics_metrics.description: Yale punted 27 times to Princeton’s 40 and showed an average gain of close to four yards in each exchange of punts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include number of punts and average gains/returns to indicate field-position battle and special teams effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties (number and yards lost)
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties were numerous throughout the four periods, Yale losing 80 yards in eight setbacks to Princeton’s 60 in seven infringements of the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report penalty counts and yards — they materially affect field position and can be cited as reasons for swings in the game.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnovers and fumble recoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: Yale made three fumbles to Princeton’s one, recovering one to Princeton’s two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for turnovers and recoveries; fumbles can negate statistical superiority or be cited as decisive errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-play tactics and deception (formation and play switching)
rubrics_metrics.description: An attack in which the blue backfield passed the ball from player to player in runs around the end and then suddenly switched to long forward passes, appeared to bewilder and dazzle the Tiger line and secondary defense, just as much as the crimson’s close formation and concealed ball offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe noteworthy strategic choices (shifts, concealed-ball, unexpected switches between run/pass); highlight how tactics affected opponent confusion or success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coaching generalship and play selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Glick’s generalship was execrable upon many occasions... instead of going outside tackle, Princeton essayed a series of centre bucks which every Princeton scout must have told Glick could not succeed against Yale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate coaches' tactical choices and in-game adjustments; cite specific questionable decisions and what alternatives (e.g., off-tackle, sweeps) may have been preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ball pursuit, tackling and following the ball
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Yale was vastly superior to Princeton was in following the ball and in holding it... the close, unerring following of the ball and the splendid spirit of the players individually, and as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess team's effort plays: pursuit, tackling, holding ground — qualitative descriptions complement statistics and explain why one side prevailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual player performance (penetration, line plunging, end runs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capt Ballin was... a tower of strength. E. Trenkmann also played a splendid game, both these men frequently penetrating the blue backfield and stopping rushes... Dickerman and Glick showed remarkable ability in line plunging and end runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight standout individual plays/skills — ability to penetrate backfield, effective plunges, end runs — with examples of impact on the game.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterback management and judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Quarterback Wilson handled his team cleverly and selected plays with splendid judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on QB's game management: play calls, selection under pressure, and leadership; use examples where QB decisions produced scoring or preserved position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punting and drop-kicking proficiency (special teams scoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Yale’s first goal was clean and untarnished. Guernsey kicked it from the fifty-three-yard line... Guernsey is a toe artist of real stature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit kickers for long field goals and consistent punting; describe successful kicks and how they affected scoring or field position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to rules and errors causing penalties (procedural mistakes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brown... committed the gross and inexcusable error of speaking to Capt. Glick before reporting to the referee. The referee promptly and justly set Princeton back fifteen yards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note rule infractions and procedural errors that led to penalties and shifted momentum; explain their immediate consequences (e.g., loss of yardage, turnover).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive formation effectiveness (adaptation to opponent passes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Yale’s basket formation for forward-pass defence, four men back, was well conceived... but her normal defensive arrangement of backs, three abreast, twelve yards back, is open to grave criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate defensive alignments and how they handle opponent tactics (forward pass, off-tackle); mention when formations succeed or leave vulnerabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clutch plays and missed opportunities (drops, bounds, timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore’s catch glanced from his fingers... He still had time to pick it up on the bound and score; the oval hit his knee and bounded over the side-line, in touch. Right there waned and flickered Princeton’s last hope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call out decisive missed catches, drops, or bounces that changed the outcome; contrast with successful clutch plays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching control and effectiveness (walks, wildness, hits with men on)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cheney was wild and ineffective... Tesreau, the New York pitcher, was very wild, but the Chicago batsmen could not hit him with men on bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In baseball recaps report pitcher control: walks, hit batters, wildness, and whether pitchers allowed hits with runners on; these determine runs allowed and inning outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catcher/fielding miscues (passed balls, errors leading to runs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Archer, the Chicago catcher, had a bad day. Five bases were stolen on him, and he had two passed balls, one of which let in a run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document passed balls, errors, and their direct scoring consequences; assess catcher’s handling and its effect on opponent base-stealing and runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fielding quality (throws to bases, ground-covering, catches)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shore... with the assistance of some clever throwing to second by Forrest Cady and grand ground-covering by the Boston outfield... The best fielding features were furnished by Bush, who displayed remarkable ability in covering ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight defensive excellence — timely throws, range, double plays, and catches that saved runs — as central elements of game storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clustering of hits and timely batting (bunching of hits, clutch singles/doubles)
rubrics_metrics.description: The champions bunched their three hits with his two passes for four runs... Herzog made two doubles and a single in four times up, and was responsible for five of the New York runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note when hits cluster with walks to produce multiple runs; single out batters who delivered multiple or timely hits that produced scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base running/steals and daring (stolen bases, audacious plays)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stolen bases—Burns, Merkle 2, Murray, Herzog. Ty Cobb... daring base running... Will Cobb have the nerve to try to steal home? You said it; he will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe aggressive base running and steals as momentum-changing actions; colorful anecdotes of daring (e.g., attempts to steal home) enrich copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Umpiring and officiating influence
rubrics_metrics.description: He was given what belonged to him by Umpire Evans... Caldwell was put out of the game for being mad because Cobb had outwitted him. Umpires—Rigler and Byron.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge key umpire/referee decisions that influenced the game, including disputed rulings and enforcement of rules, and their effect on team reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training regimen and coach's team-building (crew development)
rubrics_metrics.description: Daily work on the machines will then be ordered... Rice is confronted with a difficult task this season in finding the material to build up a winning crew... In years past Coach Rice has started out the season with an untrained and comparatively small squad of oarsmen and has startled college circles with a wonderful eight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For preview pieces, evaluate coaching plans and training schedules (daily machine work, developing new stroke); cite coach’s past record in transforming undertrained squads as a predictor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team spirit, determination and intangible character
rubrics_metrics.description: Through sheer spirit, through indomitable determination, through utter willingness to give the final measure of physical sacrifice... That was the spirit that won for Yale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assessments of team morale, fighting spirit, and willingness to sacrifice as explanations for outcomes beyond pure technical metrics; use vivid language to convey emotional significance.
